title: Noise budget cards and personalized channel profiles (draft)
content:
Purpose

This is a working draft exploring two linked ideas for the Alerts/Notifications surface: (A) compact "noise budget" cards that surface how close an SLO, service, or team is to their daily/weekly alert budget, and (B) "personalized channel profiles" — simple storable presets that determine how a user/team receives signals (channels, quiet windows, escalation path). Goal is to reduce noise, make on-call tuning faster, and give non-SRE stakeholders confidence in what will reach them.

Context and design goals
- Problem: teams keep creating ad-hoc thresholds and channel fanouts; product teams then get noisy notifications and re-create filters in Slack.
- Objective: make it fast to see why you were paged, how noisy a rule is, and change delivery for you or for the whole team with a click.
- Constraints: preserve per-tenant/route RBAC, keep default templates simple, integrate with existing escalation and channel infra (pager, slack, email, webhook).

Primary personas
- On-call engineer (SE/SRE): cares about latency and error-rate SLOs, needs low-latency channel options (pager, SMS), and wants a quick way to silence noisy rules during maintenance.
- Product manager: cares about business-impact SLOs and wants digest options (daily digest + top offenders).
- Engineering manager / stakeholder: wants summary-level alerts and ability to opt into major incident channels only.

Noise budget cards — concept
- Card = 1 compact row representing: service/route, SLO name, current burn %, trend sparkline (last 24h), top contributing alert rules, "actions" menu.
- Color rules: <30% green, 30-70% amber, 70-100% red, >100% pulsing red.
- Hover / expand: shows most recent alert instances (time, rule, channel used, annotated impact).
- Click through: opens the rule composer with a preview of examples and a toggle to route to a different profile.
- Use cases: quick triage during morning check-ins, auto-generated weekly digest email, incident retros where you can filter by high burn cards.

Wireframe notes (high level)
- Left column: sticky filters (team, region, product, time window, severity).
- Main area: grid of noise budget cards (compact) with option to pin 0-5 to top as "watchlist".
- Top toolbar: date-window picker, synthetic-incident simulator (button), "apply profile to selection" CTA.
- Card actions: mute-rule, snooze-service (1hr,4hr,custom), open-playbook, re-route (open profile chooser), estimate-cost (tokens/ops impact).

Personalized channel profiles — concept
- Small named presets users can create/save and share: e.g., "immediate-pager", "digest-only", "critical-only-v2", "weekend-filter".
- A profile contains: allowed channels, severity threshold, quiet-hours (local tz), escalation sequence (if primary fails), suppression rules (if incident labeled maintenance), and preferred notification format (short vs full message).
- Profiles can be applied at three scopes: personal, team-default (requires permission), route/rule-level override.
- Quick UI: profile pill in user avatar menu for fast swap (switch to "digest-only" when off-call).

Behavioral rules and UX edge cases
- Conflict resolution: rule-level explicit routing > team-default profile > personal profile. If someone pins a personal profile, show a subtle banner telling them they will override team defaults in their inbox.
- Quiet-hours: local timezone by default; allow service-level timezone if service spans region.
- Progressive suppression: when a rule generates >X alerts in Y minutes for same owner, system suggests moving rule to a lower fanout or creating a suppression window — propose via inline CTA ("Auto-suppress noisy rule").
- Synthetic preview: before applying a profile broadly, run against last 48h and show count delta for each channel (how many fewer Slack pings, how many more digests).

Backlog & MVP scope (proposal)
- M0 (minimal viable): noise budget card list view (read-only), basic profile UI (create/save personal), apply profile to self only, snooze per-card, baked-in filters, and synthetic preview for 24h.
- M1: team-default profiles with permission checks, card expand with last 10 alerts, pin-to-watchlist, quick re-route to different channel from card actions.
- M2: auto-suppress suggestion engine, cost-estimate per-rule, integration with rollouts (auto-suppress during canary windows), shareable profile templates and API to set profile programmatically.

Acceptance criteria (for M0)
- Users can see noise budget cards for their teams and services and sort by burn %.
- Users can create a personal profile and apply it to themselves; profile takes effect within 30s for new alerts.
- Card snooze prevents notifications to the user's personal channels for the snooze duration.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- Should noise budget be per-SLO only, or also per-alert-rule? (Pros: SLO is higher-level. Cons: need to attribute rule -> SLO automatically).
- How aggressive should auto-suppression suggestions be? (risk: masking real incidents vs benefit: lower pager noise).
- API-first: expose profiles in API for infra automation vs GUI-only to keep adoption manual. Recommend API-first but gated by RBAC.

Short-term design tasks
- Low-fi wireframes for: card grid, expanded card modal, profile editor, and synthetic-preview modal (owner: Priya).
- Flow spec: apply profile -> preview -> confirm -> apply to scope (owner: Ethan).
- Backend: schema for profile (channels[], thresholds, quiet_hours[], escalation_sequence[]), endpoints for preview and apply (owner: SRE infra eng TBD).

Notes to reviewers
- This doc focuses on reducing noise for people; not trying to redesign escalation engine. Keep idea surface small for M0. Please add comments inline (use sticky notes in the prototype) where you think policy or RBAC will block implementation.

Short checklist before next sync
- [ ] Low-fi mockups uploaded to GH prototype (link above)
- [ ] Product PRD sketch complete for M0 (include metrics: reduction in page volume, profile adoption rate)
- [ ] Engineering spike: synthetic-preview run on 2 services to validate count deltas

Quick links and refs
- Jira: PRODOPS-1234 (profile API), UX-706 (card grid mockups)
- Confluence: Notification Patterns (linked)
- Prototype: github.com/redwood-inference/console-prototypes/pull/98

-- end of draft --

(Notes: drafting informal, meant for internal review. Expect many TODOs and questions. Prioritize actionable M0 items for next sprint.)
